newsitem.title: UK: N. Sea drilling above 1995 levels so far this year.
newsitem.headline: N. Sea drilling above 1995 levels so far this year.

text.p: Overall North Sea exploration and appraisal drilling levels for the year to date are five percent higher than in 1995, with the U.K.'s West of Shetlands sector seeing the largest number of spuds in the third quarter, consultants Arthur Andersen said.

"By the end of September, 65 exploration wells had spudded compared with 62 in the same period of 1995. If this trend continues, this year could see the highest level of drilling since 1993," Arthur Andersen said in their third quarter review.
Out of a total of 27 well starts in third quarter 1996, seven were in the West of Shetlands.
This compares with five spuds in the northern, central and southern North Sea basins, the report said.

"The high level of activity in the West of Shetlands area shows that operators are keen to explore this frontier region and many of the wells (four out of seven) were drilled on acreage awarded in the recent 16th Round," it added.
The high level of activity was expected to continue for "a number of years to come" with West of Shetlands blocks included in the area covered by next year's 17th licensing round.
Arthur Andersen said a total of 25 wells were completed during the third quarter.
